Risk Description: Unauthorized production access due to standing admin/root privileges held by multiple engineers
Existing Controls: None — access is permanent and unreviewed
Recommended Treatment: Implement least-privilege IAM roles with time-boxed elevation (e.g. AWS IAM Identity Center session-based admin); conduct quarterly access review

Risk Description: Customer PII exposure via unmasked production data used in staging environment
Existing Controls: Staging environment access is limited to engineering staff only
Recommended Treatment: Implement data masking/synthetic data generation for all non-production environments before next data refresh

Risk Description: Undetected security incident due to absence of centralized log monitoring/SIEM
Existing Controls: Application logs exist in CloudWatch but are not actively reviewed
Recommended Treatment: Stand up a lightweight SIEM (e.g. Microsoft Sentinel or an open-source ELK stack) ingesting auth, admin-action, and infrastructure logs, with basic alerting rules

Risk Description: Prolonged unauthorized access following employee offboarding due to inconsistent de-provisioning
Existing Controls: Manual access revocation checklist exists but is not consistently followed
Recommended Treatment: Build an offboarding automation script or SSO-centric de-provisioning process covering all connected SaaS tools

Risk Description: Vulnerable dependencies or misconfigurations shipped to production due to no security testing in CI/CD
Recommended Treatment: Introduce SAST scanning and a lightweight DAST scan (see this repo's HawkScan-oriented workflow) as a required CI gate before production deploys

Risk Description: Regulatory non-compliance under India's DPDP Act due to no formal compliance mapping
Existing Controls: General awareness of DPDP obligations among leadership
Recommended Treatment: Commission a DPDP-specific gap assessment and appoint a designated data protection point of contact

Risk Description: Business disruption from unrecoverable data loss due to untested disaster-recovery process
Recommended Treatment: Document and test a formal disaster-recovery runbook, including a scheduled annual restore test

Risk Description: Credential compromise due to inconsistent MFA enforcement across tools
Existing Controls: MFA is available but optional on most tools
Recommended Treatment: Mandate MFA org-wide via Google Workspace admin policy and SSO enforcement on all connected applications

Risk Description: Successful phishing attack against staff due to no security awareness training
Recommended Treatment: Roll out a baseline security-awareness training module and a simple internal reporting channel for suspicious emails

Risk Description: Undetected supplier-side data breach due to no vendor security due-diligence process
Existing Controls: Vendors are selected based on functional fit only
Recommended Treatment: Introduce a basic vendor security questionnaire for any supplier handling customer data

Risk Description: Inability to reconstruct an incident timeline due to inconsistent authentication/admin-action logging
Recommended Treatment: Extend logging coverage to authentication events and administrative actions across all production systems

Risk Description: Segregation-of-duties failure allowing a single engineer to introduce and deploy malicious or flawed code unreviewed
Existing Controls: Pull requests are used but approval is not strictly enforced
Recommended Treatment: Enforce mandatory second-reviewer approval and branch protection rules on the production deployment branch
